title: Ginject Performance Characteristics
purpose: Document performance bottlenecks and optimization opportunities

dependency_resolution.mitigation: use fewer parameters, cache handler signatures (already done)

exception_handling.issue: panic recovery + stack trace capture expensive
exception_handling.mitigation: avoid exceptions in hot path, use bool returns

middleware_chain.mitigation: keep middleware count low (2-3 global max)

json_marshaling.mitigation: use binary format for high-throughput APIs

websocket_fanout.mitigation: use topic patterns to reduce subscribers

bootstrap_module_name_resolution.issue: go/parser invoked at runtime to name modules for logs
bootstrap_module_name_resolution.cost: ~64% of framework bootstrap before the fix; ~100us per module before memoisation
bootstrap_module_name_resolution.mitigation: frame skipping + (file,line) memoisation applied; consider resolving Name lazily in Listen instead

nested_module_di.issue: providers copied upward, so each module re-resolves the accumulated set
nested_module_di.cost: O(P^2) for deep import chains; 18.0ms for a 200-deep chain
nested_module_di.mitigation: hoisting dedup applied; a shared provider registry would be needed for O(P+D)

opportunity_2.name: Cache route-specific handler chains
opportunity_2.current: already composed per route pattern at app.Create; Router.Match returns the whole handler chain in one lookup

opportunity_5.name: Slow-client handling on WS writes
opportunity_5.current: 32-message buffer plus a write deadline (WSConfig.WriteTimeout, default 10s); write failure closes the conn to force teardown
opportunity_5.status: DONE - a stalled peer no longer pins the write goroutine

opportunity_6.name: Lazy Module.Name resolution
opportunity_6.current: resolved eagerly in Build(), used only by Listen's InstanceLoader log
opportunity_6.potential_savings: the remaining ~0.4ms of cold-start parse cost, and it would also stop silently yielding "" in -trimpath builds

throughput.broker_publishes_per_second: not benchmarked end-to-end; memorybroker.Publish itself measured in isolation at ~18-24 microseconds/op fanning out to 1000 exact-topic subscribers, ~2 microseconds/op for 10 mixed exact+prefix+global subscribers (see memorybroker/broker_bench_test.go) — do not cite a messages/sec figure without re-measuring, this field previously stated an unverified 100K-1M

optimization_checklist: [ ] Profile actual hot paths before optimizing
[ ] Use topic patterns to reduce WS fanout
[ ] Avoid exceptions in normal flow (use bool returns)
[ ] Keep global middleware count low (2-3 max)
[ ] Use binary serialization for high-throughput APIs
[ ] Batch database operations instead of per-request queries
measurement_environment: Intel i7-9750H @ 2.60GHz, darwin/amd64, go1.25.5. All figures below are measured, not estimated; figures elsewhere in this file that read as ranges are estimates.

root_cause_of_the_slow_sample.attribution: 99.94% of it was ONE call: catalog.StoreService.NewProvider -> categories().Schema(), loading and indexing 195MB of stale seed data left in sample/data/shop/categories
root_cause_of_the_slow_sample.lesson: separate external-IO time from framework time before optimising anything. Module discovery, DI and reflection were NOT the cause

module_name_resolution.what: moduleBuilder.Build -> resolveModuleName walks the call stack and runs go/parser on each frame file, only to produce Module.Name for the InstanceLoader log line
module_name_resolution.measured: 2.81ms of the 4.00ms framework bootstrap = 64%. 14 .go files parsed, 2.59ms of that in parser.ParseFile
module_name_resolution.pprof: moduleNameCandidatesAtLine 38.98% cum, of which go/token.FileSet.Position alone 32.20% (two Position calls per declaration, per frame, per Build)
module_name_resolution.natural_experiment: building with -trimpath makes every parse fail: App.Create drops 4.00ms -> 1.62ms and every Module.Name becomes empty
module_name_resolution.production_caveat: source is read by absolute compile-time path, so in a container or a -trimpath binary resolution silently yields "" and Listen logs no InstanceLoader lines at all
fixes_applied: skip frames in package core except _test.go files (core never declares a user module)
memoize the AST scan by (file, line, allowFuncLitMatch)
module_name_resolution.result: App.Create 4.00ms -> ~2.0ms; 200 flat modules 20.18ms -> 0.80ms (25x); Build() for 200 modules 19.78ms -> 0.53ms

di_resolution_complexity.flat_imports: O(N). injectDependencies calls = 2N. Doubling N multiplies time by 1.96-1.98
di_resolution_complexity.nested_imports: O(P^2), measured exactly: injectDependencies calls = N^2 (N=10 -> 100, N=50 -> 2500, N=200 -> 40000). Doubling N multiplies time by 3.55 -> 3.70 -> 3.95
di_resolution_complexity.mechanism: prependInjectedModules copies a child module's providers UP into its parent, so a module at depth j holds N-j providers and every module re-runs injectDependencies over its whole accumulated list
di_resolution_complexity.hoisting_fix: the hoisting block prepended duplicates without dropping the originals, so root.providers held 2N-1 entries for N providers. Deduped: chain of 200 went 31.5ms -> 18.0ms and root.providers 399 -> 200
di_resolution_complexity.still_open: complexity is still O(P^2); only a shared provider registry instead of upward copying would make it O(P+D). Irrelevant at sample scale (9 modules, 6 providers = 941us)

event_emit_contention.before: 70ns at 1 CPU -> 105ns at 4 -> 134ns at 12. Getting SLOWER with more cores is the signature of lock contention: Emit took the write lock even when no once-listener existed
event_emit_contention.after: 69ns at 1 CPU -> 68ns at 4 -> 50ns at 12. RLock fast path, positive scaling, 2.7x at 12 cores
event_emit_contention.why_it_matters: with EnableAccessLog the trace path emits several events per request, so every request serialized on that one lock

storage_table_load.problem: rebuildIndex phase 2 read and json.Unmarshal every document even with no schema registered, where updateSecondary/updateText return immediately. At 100k docs that was 466ms of pure waste out of 840ms
storage_table_load.fix_1: guard the payload decode on idx.hasSchema(): 100k docs 1.424s -> 1.107s (-22%)
storage_table_load.fix_2: OpenWithSchemas / StoreModuleOptions.Schemas pre-declare the schema so one pass builds primary+secondary+text: 839ms -> 683ms (-19%). Measured, smaller than a naive 2-pass-to-1-pass estimate because the surviving pass is the expensive one

measured_baselines.storage_tx_commit: ~18-21ms/op for BenchmarkTx_2Inserts / Update / Delete alike. Entirely fsync-bound: the numbers do not move with the amount of work, so index bookkeeping inside a Tx is not worth optimising
